requirement: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.index.chapter`. I judged this from the supplied test source alone and requested no implementation source.

**Directive form (MAY, standalone, empty body, at least three colons, closing at least as long as opening)**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[marker_accepts_long_fences_and_ignores_examples]` accepts a four-colon directive.
- It accepts a four-colon opener closed by five colons.
- It rejects a missing closing fence.
- It rejects a non-empty body.
- It rejects a closing fence shorter than the opening one (`::::` opened, `:::` closed).
- It ignores a two-colon form.
- It ignores an inline, non-standalone occurrence.
- It ignores markers inside a code fence and inside a `{req}` example.
- The assertions check the exact matched range and the error cases.

**At most one directive per book**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[repeated_index_markers_fail_with_a_clear_error]` covers two markers in separate chapters.
- It also covers two markers in the same chapter.
- Both cases assert an error containing "only one".
- The code-fence and example markers in the marker test show that literal occurrences are not counted as extra directives.

**Index lists all requirements, each linking to its detail page**
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` defines five requirements.
- For each, it finds the table row linking to `requirements-index/<name>.html`.
- It asserts the state column for each row.
- It checks that the table is aligned.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers requirements and examples, including a nested child chapter. It asserts the link targets and detail-page names.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` covers links from definitions in other chapters to the index's detail pages.
- Detail-page generation and its format belong to `requirements.index.detail_pages`, which is cited here and has its own tests.

**Directive replaced with the table**
- The explicit-marker tests assert that `{requirements-index}` is absent from the index content.
- They assert that table rows are present.
- `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` asserts that the explicit index keeps its placement. The book has 3 items, so no default chapter is appended.

**Otherwise generate the default chapter**
- `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` asserts that a default chapter is appended as the last top-level item.
- Its name is "Requirements index" and its path is `requirements-index.md`.
- It has no source path and no parent names.
- Its section number is 3, one more than the largest numbered chapter (2).
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` covers a book with no definitions, both with and without prose chapters.
- That test asserts section number 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
- It asserts a nonempty table header and that no source file is written.
- It checks that a marker inside a code block in the prose does not suppress the default chapter and that the prose is left unchanged.

I found no unreviewed obligation, boundary or failure case. The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.

When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
